en: Now, a couple of useful shortcuts for
working in the input field here.
If you're typing something and you wanna
clear that, you can quickly hit Ctrl+C to do
so. What's also useful to know is that if
you hit Escape twice here, you'll open this
picker, which allows you to move through
your session
and go back to an earlier
state, but That's something we'll get back
to later actually because
navigating the session tree is a very
powerful feature of Py and it's worth a
closer look. So we'll dive in deeper into
that later.
I already showed you that you can quit a
session by typing
/quit, but you can also hit Ctrl+D
to close it
and then resume it with py
-c, for example, to continue that last
session you worked in.
And if you want to enter a multiline,
message.
You can use Shift+Enter in most terminals,
but if that does not work, if that does send
the message instead, you can try Ctrl+J.
That should then do the trick.
Also worth noting, if you get back a
response from the agent, like here,
this summary, and you want to use that
somewhere else, you want to post it on
social media, or maybe you want to take it
to ChatGPT, to the web app, to get a another
opinion on what you're building.
So you want to copy this.
You can of course highlight this
like that and press Command+C or Control+C,
whatever the default shortcut on your
operating system is, to copy that. But there
is an even easier way by just typing /copy,
and that will copy the last agent message to
the clipboard. And that's very convenient,
especially for longer outputs. So that's
something worth knowing about. And then last
but not least, if you want to paste
something in here like this BetterAuth
documentation here,
you can use Command+V, Control+V, whatever
the default is on your operating system. But
if you want to paste in an image, which also
is supported if the model you selected has
vision capabilities. So if I want to paste
in a screenshot here, let's say taking a
little screenshot here of this part of the
page.
Command+V on macOS will not work, but
Control+V will. And that may look weird,
this output here, but in the end, what
happens is
Pi will temporarily save that
screenshot, which you may have had in your
clipboard, into a temporary file on your
system and paste in that path to that file.
And that way, the agent and the model will
be able to view it. So Control+V for
inserting images.
